industry: Cleaning (house cleaning, carpet/rug) and pressure/soft washing
words_and_claims_to_avoid: Government look-alike design, 'official notice', fake checks or invoices (39 USC 3001)
Unsubstantiated 'best', '#1', 'voted #1', 'guaranteed results', percent-savings claims (FTC Act s.5)
Invented or composite testimonials, star ratings or review counts (16 CFR 255)
'Free' unless it truly costs nothing and carries no hidden obligation (16 CFR 251)
Fake expiration dates or fake scarcity; any deadline printed must be real
Demographic/age targeting language (e.g., 'seniors', 'retirees') unless the client has evidence it fits their actual buyers
Any vendor case-study result (calls, ROI, revenue) printed as if it were the client's own result
'Sanitized', 'disinfected', 'kills 99.9% of germs', 'antibacterial', 'allergen-free' unless the client uses an EPA-registered product for that use and the claim matches its label (40 CFR 152.15)
'Healthy home' or health benefits (GOLD-002 'key to a healthy home') unless substantiated
'Kills mold/algae/moss' for soft washing unless the product is registered for it and the client meets state applicator rules (pesticidal claim)
'Eco-friendly', 'green', 'biodegradable', 'non-toxic', 'safe for plants/pets' without specific substantiation (16 CFR 260)
'Get your deposit back' (outcome the cleaner doesn't control)
'Licensed, bonded and insured' unless all three are true
AI-looking photos passed off as the client's own work (GOLD-007 looks AI-generated): before/after must be real
compliance_notes: Any discount or 'save X%' must be off a real, recently charged price; 'save 40%' with no reference price is not allowed.

FTC 'Free' Guide, 16 CFR 251 (verified): (1) 'free with purchase' means the paid item is at its regular price (sold openly for about 30 days), with no markup or downgrade to cover the free item; (2) all conditions go right next to the offer, not in an asterisk footnote; (3) if the main job is priced by negotiation or bid, 'free [item] with purchase' is improper; (4) don't run the same 'free' offer more than 6 months in any 12; (5) 'gift' or 'bonus' wording doesn't cure a deceptive 'free'.
Testimonials and star ratings must be real, typical and current; disclose any material connection (16 CFR 255).

FTC Green Guides, 16 CFR 260 (verified; they cover claims about services too): unqualified 'eco-friendly', 'green' or 'environmentally safe' claims are deceptive (260.4); qualify to a specific, provable benefit (e.g., 'We donate usable furniture to [named charity]'). 'Recyclable', 'biodegradable' and similar claims have their own tests (260.8, 260.12).

Antimicrobial/mold claims (verified product rule): claiming that cleaning sanitizes, disinfects or kills germs, mold or algae is a pesticidal claim; products must be EPA-registered for that use and claims must match the label. How strictly this applies to a service company's own ad copy is a counsel question, so default to outcome language ('fresh', 'spotless', 'like new').
Before/after photos are implied performance claims (FTC Act s.5): must be real, typical and not edited to exaggerate.
Some states license pressure-washing chemical application (algaecides) as pesticide work; not verified state by state: client must confirm.
Veteran/first-responder/essential-worker discounts are fine; define eligibility and verification on the card.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, disgust, joy, pride, status, relief are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle and combo carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency/vendor-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-002 'Clean, sanitized floors are the key to a healthy home!' vs EPA pesticidal-claim rule and FTC substantiation
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: drop 'sanitized' and 'healthy home' unless label-backed and substantiated; sell 'fresh, spotless floors you love walking on'.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Soft-wash marketing 'eco-friendly / kills mold and algae' vs Green Guides (16 CFR 260) and FIFRA
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: qualify any environmental claim specifically, and only make kill claims with a registered product used per label.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-007 'We love your home like it's our own' with an AI-looking photo vs real-photo before/after rule
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Real photos win: AI or stock imagery must not look like the client's own work. The warm headline is fine.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-004 'FREE driveway cleaning with purchase of a roof cleaning' vs 16 CFR 251 when roof cleaning is quoted per job
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: use 'FREE' only with a published regular price; otherwise 'included'.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Vendor ROI figures (e.g., GOLD-007 1,520%, GOLD-008 670%) vs never printing unverified numbers
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Unaudited vendor claims; weak evidence only.
